note: Re-judged 2026-10-19 (independent auditor, after 2a5ac0ce0b). RFC 4659 Section 3.2.1.1: "The link-local address shall be included in the Next Hop field if and only if the advertising BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the peer the route is being advertised to [BGP-IPv6]." and "In all other cases, a BGP speaker shall advertise to its peer in the Next Hop Network Address field only the global IPv6 address of the next hop." Since 990744517c (owner decision 2026-10-19, rfc-gap-difficulty-2026-10-18 #22) linkLocalConditionFor gives AFI 2/SAFI 128 the peer-only condition and every other family RFC 2545 Section 3's joint one; linkScope.holdsCommonSubnet answers it from peerOnLink and linkLocalNextHop still requires a speaker-owned global and a configured link-local. Paths traced: (1) configured: sendStaticRoutes/Grouped/withdraw pass route.Family() to linkLocalNextHopFor, buildStaticRouteUpdateNew -> vpnNextHopOctets/buildMPReachVPN write 24 or 48 with zero RDs, then the session gate re-applies the decision; (2) API: AnnounceNLRIBatch -> exportFilterForBody -> normalizeOrdinaryNextHop routes 24/48-octet SAFI 128 fields to normalizeVPNNextHop -> applyEgressNextHopScope(fam); (3) relayed: both forwarding rails call applyEgressNextHopScope, which raises a zero-RD 24-octet field for a speaker-owned global on the peer's subnet and trims a 48-octet pair only off it (link-local-only unspecified-global exception kept); (4) next-hop self and (5) explicit: applyLinkLocalNextHop decides the VPN pair on linkLocalConditionPeer independently of nhMode, vpnIPv6NextHop slices nhVPNPair[:48] or [:24]; (6) default route: sendDefaultOriginateRoutes always calls BuildUnicast with SAFI unset, so it emits no VPN-IPv6 route and this requirement has no default-route path (a VPN family passes the peer-only condition into a plain IPv6 body, but exportFilterForBody -> normalizeOrdinaryNextHop trims the 32-octet form on RFC 2545's joint condition). Peer.SendAnnounce has no non-test caller. Tagged units: TestRFC4659VPNv6LinkLocalLoopbackGlobal (new: loopback global off the shared /64, 48 octets on configured, relay, next-hop-self; 24 off-link), TestRFC4659StaticVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659APIVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6LinkLocalCommonSubnet, TestRFC4659ForwardVPNv6NextHopRewriteCarriesRD, test/encode/rfc4659-vpnv6-link-local-off-subnet.ci (now the 48-octet positive with the 24-octet form rejected); each asserts the exact field. Discrimination records (rfc/discrimination/rfc4659.json) are whole-body panics re-recorded by 990744517c; the checkVPNFRR tags carry none (two producers). Auditor overlay mutants (tags ze_core ze_bgp, go test -overlay), all killed: old joint rule for VPN (loopback test configured/relay/next-hop-self red, plus untagged RFC2545ReceivedPairSubnetConditions/vpn/global-off-link); never-48 (static, API, forward, rewrite, loopback tagged tests red); always-48 regardless of subnet (static, API, forward, rewrite, loopback off-link red); and the contrast mutant giving plain IPv6 the peer-only condition (RFC2545 unicast/global-off-link and second-address tests red). Baseline green. The RFC 2545 contrast is correct per its own text, Section 3: "if and only if the BGP speaker shares a common subnet with the entity identified by the global IPv6 address carried in the Network Address of Next Hop field and the peer the route is being advertised to" (not judged here). Interop: 2a5ac0ce0b's checkVPNFRR positive (BIRD 2.15.1 holds Ze global plus link-local, both RDs zero) is a genuine independent receiver; its negative is NOT this requirement's negative: BIRD and FRR share the lab /64 with Ze, so the omitted link-local there is the speaker-owned/third-party gate, a neighbouring rule (RFC 2545 third-party gap), not "no common subnet". Residuals, not defects under the owner's reading: a third-party global sent to an on-link peer leaves without the speaker's link-local, which the iff's inclusion clause read alone would demand; Section 3.2.1.1 describes the global as "the global IPv6 address of the advertising BGP speaker", so the section does not contemplate it and the owner's #22 decision covers only the speaker's own global (open owner question). The .ci and the interop scenario were not re-run by this auditor. The encode fixture's common subnet is ::1/128.
